text:
sam_support: Heads-up — customer Janet (acct: acme-prod) reports increased tail latency and occasional 502s. Console shows region: eu-west-1 but trace headers and request logs show serving region: us-east-1. Ticket #8821 linked: https://redwood/support/tickets/8821

janet_acme: Repro steps I ran: 1) curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \nresponse included header x-serving-region: us-east-1 and body latency ~240ms. Console still highlights EU. Noticed a few auth failures earlier today too.

sam_support: Thanks Janet, can you paste one full request_id from the response headers? We need a concrete example to lookup.

janet_acme: request-id: req_2026_04_12_5567. Also saw some 403s for a minute at 08:12 UTC.

maya_ops: Looking at routing logic — we have smart-routing + fallback. If eu-west capacity is saturated for that model variant we route to nearest compatible (often us-east). Console region label is derived from account primary region, not last-serving-region. That mismatch is known but should be documented.

igor_infra: Pulling logs for req_2026_04_12_5567 — confirmed served from us-east-1 at 08:12:34. There was a transient autoscaler eviction in eu-west and a canary that spiked memory; autoscaler throttled new pods for ~40s, requests spilled to us-east.

sam_support: That matches customer report. Why did console still show eu-west? Should it show serving region per-request in the UI?

maya_ops: Current console design shows configured primary region and a small serving breakdown only on aggregated telemetry. It doesn't show per-request serving region in the session view. We can surface \"served_from\" header if we include it in logs exposed to UI.

janet_acme: From a customer perspective this is confusing — we paid for eu-west reserved capacity and everything pointing to EU. Extra cross-pop egress costs and added latency. Can we get an explanation and a mitigation?

igor_infra: Short term: set routing policy override to strict-region for that account (forces failures instead of cross-region fallback). Command we can run: \n```\nredwoodctl accounts update acme-prod --routing-policy strict-region --region eu-west-1\n```\nThat will make requests fail fast if capacity isn't available instead of spilling.

sam_support: Filed follow-up with billing and tagging team to estimate cross-region egress for acme-prod during the incident window. CC @billing.

deploy-bot: automated-alert: eu-west-1 autoscaler experienced memory pressure spike at 2026-04-12T08:12:30Z; fallback routing engaged (count=312 requests)

maya_ops: Action items: 1) Ops to share timeline + logs with customer (igor) 2) Product to clarify UI language about console region vs serving region (sam -> product) 3) Optionally enable per-request served-region header visible in the session logs (tiny SDK change) 4) Billing to estimate cross-region impact.

igor_infra: I'll attach the raw serving logs and the autoscaler traces to the ticket. Quick repro we used: \n```\ncurl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Request-Id: req_2026_04_12_5567\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"latency test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\n# look for X-Serving-Region and X-Request-Id in response headers\n```

sam_support: Thanks — I'll send an interim note to Janet with the workaround (strict-region override) and ETA for UI clarification.

janet_acme: Appreciate the quick response. Please include any logs that show the 403s we saw earlier; that one broken minute caused a bunch of retries from our side.

maya_ops: We'll also propose a console UX change: show small per-request badge when serving != primary region + a tooltip explaining fallback behavior. I'll draft a brief RFC.

igor_infra: Note for postmortem: consider increasing warm pool or pre-warming model variants in eu-west to reduce spillover for reserved accounts.

sam_support: Closing loop here, will update ticket when billing numbers and logs attached. :thumbsup:
